correctness.rationale: A left-minimal two-symbol interval starts at the last letter of one binary constant run and ends anywhere in the next run, giving \(L_w(h)=\sum_{i\ge2}\mathbf 1_{2\le h\le a_i+1}\). First differences give the number of noninitial runs and the multiplicities of their lengths, except the unique endpoint case with noninitial length \(n-1\), detected by \(\Delta(2)=1\) with no later negative differences. Any integer partition with total at most \(n-1\) is realized by an initial run of leftover length and alternating subsequent runs. Permuting those runs yields \(2k!/\prod_j m_j!\) words per ordinary nonempty profile (two words for empty and exceptional). Distinct positive lengths cost at least \(k(k+1)/2\), yielding the sharp bound and 2k! critical examples. The dependency-free program independently enumerated all 65,534 binary words through \(n=15\) and compared window counts, partitions, complete fiber multisets and maximum d. Tests corroborate rather than prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The directly inspected co-occurrence papers analyze minimal-interval structure and general sparse-output algorithms, but do not state a bijection of all binary full left-minimal answer profiles with partitions of integers 0..n−1, classify each profile fiber, or give the exact finite-length maximum of nonzero differences. The OEIS value sequence is independently known, so originality attaches to the query-profile interpretation and the complete fibers, not the integer-partition arithmetic. Actual indexed research queries on these objects returned only different problems or broader bounds. This remains a best-knowledge, not independent exhaustive, literature judgment.

value.rationale: The exact number of realizable full answer profiles is the noiseless distinguishability capacity of this natural query observation, and the explicit fiber sizes quantify all inverse ambiguity classes rather than just the number of outcomes. The partition bijection gives a complete infinite-length structural classification with an exact generating function and explicit finite-length support thresholds, directly motivated by the sparse-output representation problem of the 2022 primary paper.
